title: Training & Capability Gaps — Staff cannot execute IAM consistently
rootCause: Staff have not received structured role-based training since onboarding. Tool proficiency gaps on PL24 and AOS mean staff default to manual workarounds. Product knowledge is insufficient to confidently recommend BMW parts over non-OEM alternatives during IR interactions. Without this capability even motivated staff cannot execute IAM effectively. Per Ticket 15 (Dealer Coaching) a structured on-site coaching session is the required intervention.
impact: Capability gaps are the primary drag on all KPIs — PL24 at 61% AOS at 68% sales at 74% of target

title: Parts Basket Not Aligned to Local Car Park — 5 families missing from AOS
rootCause: The Düsseldorf car park skews toward older F-series and G-series vehicles with high demand for wear and maintenance parts. The AOS basket has not been reviewed against this profile — 5 high-demand families including engine oil, suspension components, brake discs, timing belts, and coolant are missing. Peter Lang confirmed in February that he was unsure which families to prioritise.
impact: +€3640/month estimated if basket is aligned to local car park demand

title: IAM Value Proposition — Staff unable to communicate BMW parts advantage to IRs
rootCause: Staff default to price comparisons when speaking to IRs rather than leading with quality, compatibility, and warranty arguments. This is a product knowledge and sales capability gap — not a pricing problem. BMW IAM Toolbox product argumentation materials exist but have not been introduced to the team.
impact: IR retention risk — IRs choosing non-OEM on price alone when BMW parts are competitively positioned on total value
